sessions.notes_text:
I called Elisha Patterson to apply for funding to reinstate his license and to build his resume. He logged into his SCDMV account and texted me screenshots of the reinstatement fees he owes, which are two fees of $100 and $200. I submitted a Rainy Day Fund application for $300, to be paid directly to the DMV. He said a reinstated license would help him because he’s supposed to get a vehicle on Monday. I let him know decisions usually take 2–3 weeks and that I’ll update him when we hear back.

Details from the application: he’s 24 and lives in Charleston [verify – he gave zip 29456] with his girlfriend and his mother. He came home three days ago and has no income yet. His girlfriend does caregiving work and his mother works part-time. He isn’t a caretaker for any minor children [verify], and his foster care answer didn’t come through clearly [verify].

Resume: we went through his work history together.

Skills: carpentry, and restoration work on fire and water damage. He’s interested in getting his CDL and welding certification. He has no current certifications. Education: he left high school in 12th grade and earned his GED [verify year]. He also attended Trident Tech, possibly for plumbing [verify]. I’ll format the resume and send it to him by both text and email.

Waitlist: he’s about #2 or #3, so it should be 1–2 more weeks before he’s called in.

Follow-ups

Finish formatting the resume and send it by text and email
Track the Rainy Day Fund decision (~2–3 weeks) and update Elisha
